item.title: The Healing Pod #4 - Sound and Silence
item.description:
You do not need a quiet room to meditate. The traffic, the neighbor's dog, the hum of the fridge: sound is not the enemy of your practice, it can be one of your best anchors. In this episode we talk about why noise feels like such a problem, the half-second chasing reflex that turns every sound into a story, a different way to meet sound by receiving instead of chasing, and the quiet hiding underneath all the noise. Then we practice together for seven minutes, the same as last time. The growth this week goes into your homework instead: ten minutes a day, plus a one-minute listening assignment. Hosted by Alden Isaac.

item.title: The Healing Pod #3 - The Restless Body
item.description:
Your nose itches the moment you sit down to meditate. Your foot falls asleep, your back aches, your knee wants to bounce. That is not failure. Your body did not get louder, you got quieter, and now you can finally feel what was always there. In this episode we talk about why stillness feels wrong to the body at first, the half-second reflex between an itch and a scratch, the honest line between discomfort and real pain, and how the body becomes your meditation teacher instead of your meditation problem. Then we practice together for seven minutes, one minute longer than last time. Hosted by Alden Isaac.

item.title: The Healing Pod #2 - The Wandering Mind
item.description:
Your mind wanders during meditation. That is not a flaw, it is the workout. In this episode we talk about why your brain will not quiet down, why fighting your thoughts only makes them louder, and the one move that handles every kind of wandering: notice, name it softly, and return kindly. Then we practice together for six minutes, one minute longer than last time. Hosted by Alden Isaac.

item.title: The Healing Pod - Trailer
item.description:
Welcome to The Healing Pod. A meditation show that starts at the very beginning, with the simplest possible things, and builds episode by episode, for as long as it takes. Each episode teaches one thing and gives you one practice. No experience, no special gear, no belief system required. Hosted by Alden Isaac.
